Summarise the parameters of the movement models fitted with ctmm

Source: R/ctmm_tt_summary.R
ctmm_tt_summary.Rd

This function extracts the estimates of the parameters of the movement models fitted with ctmm_tt_fit(), with their confidence intervals (as given by summary() on each model, see ctmm::summary.ctmm()). The table has one row per track, in the same order as the table of models (and thus of the metadata), so that it can be easily joined with the metadata (e.g. to compare home range sizes between sexes).

Usage

ctmm_tt_summary(x, level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

A table of models created with ctmm_tt_fit().

level

The confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

Value

A tibble with one row per track, and columns:

  • the track id column (as in x)

  • model_name: the name of the model

  • dof_area: the effective number of degrees of freedom for the area

  • for each parameter (e.g. area, tau_position, tau_velocity, speed, diffusion), three columns with the lower bound of the confidence interval (_low), the estimate (_est) and the upper bound (_high)

Details

The parameters depend on the models: e.g. models without autocorrelation ("IID") only have an area, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck models ("OU") also have a time scale of the autocorrelation of positions (tau_position, the home range crossing time), and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck foraging models ("OUF") also have a time scale of the autocorrelation of velocities (tau_velocity), and estimates of speed. The table has columns for all the parameters estimated for any track, and NA for the tracks whose model does not estimate a parameter.

Note that area is the area of the Gaussian home range of the model (at the 95% level), which is not the same as the home range estimated with hr_tt_akde() (which uses the model to estimate the utilisation distribution non-parametrically).

The values are returned as units objects in SI units (e.g. m^2 for areas, seconds for time scales); they can be converted to more convenient units with units::set_units() (e.g. units::set_units(area_est, km^2)).

See also

ctmm_tt_fit() to fit the models.

Examples

data(buffalo, package = "ctmm")
buffalo_tt <- mt_as_move2(buffalo)
# we use a subset of the first two buffalo to make the example fast
buffalo_sub <- buffalo_tt %>%
  filter_by_meta(track %in% c("Cilla", "Gabs")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(track) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()
buffalo_fit <- ctmm_tt_fit(buffalo_sub, model = "ou")
#> Minimum sampling interval of 59 minutes in Cilla
#> Minimum sampling interval of 57 minutes in Gabs
ctmm_tt_summary(buffalo_fit)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 12
#>   track model_name     dof_area  area_low  area_est  area_high tau_position_low
#>   <fct> <chr>             <dbl>     [m^2]     [m^2]      [m^2]              [s]
#> 1 Cilla OU anisotropic     3.29 22314818. 98190277. 229207994.           25886.
#> 2 Gabs  OU anisotropic     1.68  8261023. 91503644. 272347060.           33010.
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: tau_position_est [s], tau_position_high [s],
#> #   diffusion_low [m^2/s], diffusion_est [m^2/s], diffusion_high [m^2/s]
